sections.title: Localization near the edge for the lattice Anderson-Bernoulli model on general dimension
sections.abstract: The paper proves Anderson localization near the bottom of the spectrum for the lattice Anderson model with Bernoulli potential in every dimension d≥2, completing a problem left open by Bourgain and Kenig.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim localization near the spectral edge for Bernoulli disorder in all dimensions d≥2 using a probabilistic discrete unique-continuation principle.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The lattice Anderson tight-binding model with Bernoulli potential on Z^d at the lower spectral edge, d≥2.
sections.caveat: New unrefereed preprint; the proof and the precise relation to the Bourgain–Kenig problem require expert checking.

sections.title: Stable solutions of the Allen–Cahn equation in dimension three are one-dimensional
sections.abstract: The authors claim that every bounded stable solution of the Allen–Cahn equation in R^3 is one-dimensional, implying De Giorgi's conjecture for monotone solutions in dimension four.
sections.claimed_result: Every bounded stable solution in three dimensions is one-dimensional, with the stated dimension-four consequence.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Bounded stable Allen–Cahn solutions on R^3; the consequence concerns monotone solutions in dimension four.
sections.caveat: The abstract does not expose the proof's quantitative estimates; this remains a preprint claim.

sections.title: Bounded-orbit wandering domains do not exist
sections.abstract: The paper claims that transcendental entire functions have no wandering Fatou components with bounded forward orbit, and gives a stronger meromorphic statement.
sections.claimed_result: Bounded-orbit wandering domains do not occur for transcendental entire functions; every point in a meromorphic wandering domain has an unbounded orbit, according to the authors.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Transcendental entire or meromorphic functions and their Fatou components.
sections.caveat: Independent verification remains important; a checked MathDB result labels the new claim unverified.

sections.title: Global well-posedness and scattering for the three-dimensional focusing energy-critical NLS
sections.abstract: The authors claim global well-posedness and scattering below the ground-state energy and gradient thresholds for the three-dimensional focusing energy-critical NLS.
sections.claimed_result: The paper claims to confirm the dimension-three threshold conjecture using frequency-localized L^4 estimates and an adapted interaction Morawetz identity.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The focusing energy-critical NLS in three spatial dimensions below both stated thresholds.
sections.caveat: The frequency-truncation estimates and exact threshold formulation need full-proof checking.

sections.title: Thinning and sprinkling: from robust sampling to almost Hamiltonicity
sections.abstract: The paper develops a thinning–sprinkling method for robustness under random vertex sampling and derives almost-Hamiltonicity results for several graph classes.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim cycles of length (1-o(1))n in stated polylogarithmic regimes, giving asymptotic solutions to the cited Chvátal and Lovász conjectures.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Tough graphs, connected vertex-transitive graphs, nearly regular sublinear expanders, and k-connected graphs with k=ω(log n).
sections.caveat: Almost-spanning cycles are weaker than full Hamilton cycles; the exact hypotheses and ranges require careful reading.
